subject: Oceanography
title: Sea Surface Temperature
description: Learn Sea Surface Temperature in one minute.

hook.text: Sea surface temperature (SST) is the most watched ocean metric—it drives hurricanes, rain, and fisheries.

buildup.text: Satellites measure SST globally every day—revealing warm pools, cold upwelling zones, and anomalies.

discovery.text: The warm pool in the western Pacific is Earth's largest warm water mass—fueling monsoons across Asia.

twist.text: In 2023, global SST shattered records by a huge margin—catching even climate scientists off guard.

climax.text: Higher SSTs mean more evaporation, stronger storms, and accelerating coral bleaching worldwide.

punchline.text: The ocean's skin temperature sets the mood for global weather.

quiz.question: Why does sea surface temperature matter for weather?
options: It drives evaporation, storms, and rainfall patterns
It only matters at the poles
